newsitem.title: USA: Union leader "not optimistic" about GE talks.
newsitem.headline: Union leader "not optimistic" about GE talks.

text.p: The leader of a committee of 14 unions negotiating a new contract with General Electric Co said he was "not optimistic" about the talks, with the current pact set to expire at midnight Sunday.
Ed Fire, chairman of the Coordinated Bargaining Committee, made the remark after a rally at New York's Rockefeller Center when he was asked to comment on the status of the talks.

GE and the committee, which represents 46,000 unionized workers at the company, have been negotiating for the past five weeks. The largest of the 14 unions is the International Union of Electrical Workers (IUE), which is headed by Fire.

Wages and benefits are among the issues involved in the negotiations, but the unions say their overriding concern is job security. They say union jobs at GE have fallen to their current level from 80,000 in the past 20 years as a result of plant closures in the United States. Many of those jobs have gone to other countries, particularly Mexico, they say.

Although Fire would not disclose details of the talks, other union sources said it would be highly unlikely for any GE workers to walk off their jobs Monday morning if a tentative agreement was not reached before then.
The sources said that because of procedural and voting rules within the unions, any strike probably would not occur until July 9 or July 10.

Traditionally, they said, General Electric presents its last and best offer to the unions at about a half hour before a contract expires. The sources said that it would probably take a few days to consider a last-minute offer.

"Our negotiations are continuing on schedule. We will present a comprehensive proposal to the union before the current contract expires that is fair to employees and keeps GE competitive. We are confident this will lead to a timely settlement," a GE spokesman, Ted Meyer, said in a statement.
